plan.title: How do canal locks work?
plan.businessGoal: Show, in a short demonstration module for Elabora, how an AI can build an original 3D teaching component that an author customises without code, inside a real slide-based e-learning experience.

audience.role: General public: teenagers and adults curious about canals, with no prior knowledge
audience.notes: Self-paced on the web, desktop or phone. No voice-over: every piece of information is written on screen, with discreet sound effects that can be muted.

objectives.statement: Explain why a boat changes level in a lock: water flowing from the higher canal (or towards the lower one) changes the level in the chamber, the floating boat follows that level, and a pair of gates opens only when the water is level on both sides.
objectives.criterion: Brings the boat to the upper canal in the simulation (hints allowed), then follows the three principles of the explanation.

objectives.statement: Choose, for a boat waiting in a full lock chamber, the interventions that bring it down to the lower canal, and justify each choice by the water levels on either side of the gates.
objectives.criterion: Picks the good option at both decisions of the lock keeper's case, at the first try or after one retry.

items.title: How can a boat travel uphill?
items.description: Opening slide. A little barge waits in the lower canal, facing the closed gates of a lock; behind them the upper canal sits higher. The 3D diorama appears as a watercolour wash. A short narrated hook asks how the boat could ever get up there, without giving the answer, and a Start button opens the simulation.

lockedTexts.text: Canals are flat, but the land is not. Up ahead, the water is higher, and this little barge needs to reach it. How will it get up there?

items.title: Help the boat reach the upper canal
items.description: Main slide: the learner operates the 3D lock (lower and upper gates, lower and upper paddles, the boat's moves) with controls placed above and below the diorama. Causal rules: the chamber only fills once the lower gates are shut; opening the upper paddle lets water in; the boat follows the water; a pair of gates only opens when the levels on both sides are equal. Mistakes get a visible reaction (the gates strain, the control shakes), never a penalty; screen readers hear the explanation. Progressive hints (a nudge, then what to do, then the control to use), a reset button, a view switch, a mute button and a success animation when the boat sails into the upper canal. No debrief text: once the boat is up, a button leads on to the explanation.

items.title: The secret is water, not lifting
items.description: The same lock seen in cross-section replays the ascent in short steps the learner goes through with Previous and Next, each in a bubble pointing at what moves, with a Replay button: the barge sails in; the gates close behind it; water flows down from the upper canal into the chamber; the boat floats and rises with the surface; once the levels are equal, the gates open; the barge sails out. Once the last step has played, a button leads on to the case.

items.title: Now, what if we go downhill?
items.description: Nell, the lock keeper, talks with the learner. The boat waits in a full chamber, ready to go down; the lower gates will not open. Decision 1: drain the chamber through the lower paddles (good), open both paddles to go faster (ok: the level stops halfway), force the lower gates (bad: they do not move). Decision 2, once the chamber is low: open the lower gates (good), wait a little longer (ok: nothing changes), open the upper gates (bad: they are now held shut). Every choice gets Nell's reaction, a trainer's note, and a visible consequence on the 3D lock beside the conversation. Retries allowed.

items.title: Up or down, the water does the work
items.description: Closing line once the conversation ends, on the same slide: boats go up or down because the water level changes.

lockedTexts.text: A lock doesn't lift the boat. It moves water, and the boat simply floats along. Up or down, the water level changes, so the boat changes level too.
